questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. Going too fast in a turn may cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you will get the most protection by using a helmet that:

options.text: Fits loosely.
Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Has survived a previous crash.
Provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: When you approach an octagonal sign, you must:

options.text: Slow.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually results in no difference in handling a motorcycle.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
Is encouraged to get operators used to different riding situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to a motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, you should ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It increases your line of sight.
It decreases your line of sight.
It makes it difficult to see beyond the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see farther ahead and makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to allow the wind to catch the fabric.
Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to prevent you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but also loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Making a right turn here would be unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: As your motorcycle increases speed, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals for you to go.
Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow sign means you are near a school. Be alert and ready to stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Turn off the headlight.
Follow another vehicle very closely.
Wear bright-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials to be seen by other drivers. Always use your headlight, signals, and brake light.

questions.question: Why is your lane position important when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It has little effect on whether other drivers can see you.
It is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
It cannot protect you from wind from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from nearby vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.
Apply your brakes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
Traffic flows in both directions.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows in both directions on this road.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take a breath test when an officer asks?

options.text: It is your right and there are no consequences.
It is not a serious offense.
It is recommended.
You will face legal consequences.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will face legal consequences.
questions.explanation: By driving on the road, you agree to take a chemical test if an officer asks. Refusing a test will result in at least one year of license suspension.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet or vest makes you more visible to other drivers during the day and night.

questions.question: How can you stay safer when riding at night?

options.text: Avoid riding at night.
Wear reflective clothing.
Night riding is unsafe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: Why can riding be difficult right after it starts raining?

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
The pavement becomes very slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the pavement is especially slippery. Oil from vehicles mixes with the water, creating a slippery surface.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
Pre-ride checks performed only by a mechanic.
Service only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Do not matter much since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals when you plan to change lanes or turn, even if you think no one else is nearby.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should always be the same.
Should change based on road and weather conditions.
Is not needed in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When is it important for a rider to use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly
When stopped at an intersection
When changing lanes
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket fully cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injury risk in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly without flapping in the wind.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.
Construction workers are on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Be careful because pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to turn your head if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors give you a full view of the road around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can trust other drivers to respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Is absorbed into the bloodstream very quickly.
Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.
Can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is absorbed into the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream, reaching the brain quickly.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue, you should:

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine can make fatigue worse when it wears off. Wind and weather also increase fatigue, so dress warmly and use a windshield for long rides.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together to stop. The brakes work best when used at the same time.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Red is always on top and green on the bottom of a vertical traffic light. Red is always on the left and green on the right of a horizontal traffic light.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test each brake control to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?

options.text: Price.
Protection.
Appearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is your first concern when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Always scan the road ahead and anticipate potential risks.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Don't worry about hazards because they are minimal on the roadway.
Always look ahead, but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always scan the road ahead and anticipate potential risks.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead while riding to anticipate hazards. This helps you react to problems before you reach them.

questions.question: What does research show about motorcycles with headlights on during the day?

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Other drivers are often confused.
They are less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. Motorcycles with headlights on during the day are twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up may increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Clothing that feels uncomfortable.
Clothing that provides protection in a crash.
Clothing that should not stand out to other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes provide protection in a crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding, where should your feet be?

options.text: On the gas tank.
Hanging loosely.
On the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to maintain proper balance.
